high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Opens the "Valve" for Credit Growth
high.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has implemented a series of accommodative credit policy adjustments aimed at providing additional economic growth momentum while maintaining risk control principles. Key measures implemented since the start of the year include: (1) Circular 08, which adjusts the Loan-to-Deposit Ratio (LDR) regulations; (2) Circular 25, which raises the maximum ratio of short-term capital used for medium- and long-term lending to 40%; and (3) a revised methodology for calculating credit growth that permits the exclusion of certain specialized loan balances. Most notably, the SBV has approved the exclusion of outstanding loans tied to 18 large-scale projects from major conglomerates — including Sun Group, Vingroup, and Masterise — from credit room calculations. This effectively expands available lending headroom for commercial banks without formally raising the official credit growth target. **Market implications:** This easing signals a deliberately pro-growth monetary stance. For VND traders, sustained credit expansion could place mild depreciation pressure on the dong if it widens the current account deficit. Bond investors should note that accommodative credit policy reduces urgency for rate cuts but may increase supply-side inflationary risks in H2 2026. Watch for any SBV communications on credit growth targets and potential FX intervention if lending accelerates sharply.

---

high.title: "Releasing the Credit Valve": State Bank of Vietnam Signals Injection of VND 1.5 Quadrillion into the Economy
high.summary:
In an unprecedented policy move, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued Official Document No. 5386/NHNN-TD, allowing the outstanding loans of 18 designated priority projects to be **excluded from annual credit growth room (quota) calculations**. The mechanism specifically benefits three major conglomerates — **Vingroup, Sun Group, and Masterise** — with a combined capital demand of approximately **VND 752 trillion (~USD 28 billion)** over 2026–2028. Funds are earmarked for strategic infrastructure: urban rail lines (Ben Thanh–Can Gio, Hanoi–Quang Ninh), Phu Quoc International Airport expansion, Gia Binh Airport, and other large-scale infrastructure complexes. This exemption allows commercial banks to disburse aggressively to these projects without consuming their annual credit ceilings. The SBV retains oversight by requiring separate tracking of such loan balances to ensure proper use of funds. **Market implications:** This is a structurally significant credit easing signal. A potential VND 1.5 quadrillion injection into the economy carries meaningful implications for **liquidity conditions, VND money supply growth (M2), and inflationary pressure** — all of which bear directly on SBV's future rate policy and the VND/USD trajectory. Bond investors should watch for yield curve repricing if inflation expectations rise. FX traders should monitor whether accelerated credit growth puts depreciation pressure on the VND.

---

high.title: Government Directs SBV to Study Increasing Banking System Liquidity via State Treasury Deposits
high.summary:
The Vietnamese Government has issued Resolution 168/NQ-CP (dated 27 June 2026), updating growth scenarios and priority measures for the remaining quarters of 2026, with a headline GDP growth target of 10% or above. Critically for monetary policy watchers, the Government has tasked the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) with researching mechanisms to channel State Treasury deposits into the banking system to boost liquidity — a potentially significant policy tool that could influence interbank rates and money market conditions. The resolution acknowledges headwinds from Middle East geopolitical tensions that weighed on the economy in H1 2026, while noting that key growth indicators reached multi-year or even multi-term highs, drawing positive assessments from international organizations. The dual mandate of sustaining high growth while maintaining macroeconomic stability and inflation control remains central. **For VND traders and bond investors:** expanded Treasury deposit flows into banks could ease liquidity conditions, putting downward pressure on short-term interbank rates and potentially compressing the short end of the government bond yield curve. Watch for follow-up SBV circulars or Ministry of Finance coordination announcements.

---

medium.title: Contradictory Phenomenon Unfolding in the Stock Market: What Do Experts Say?
medium.summary:
A divergence is emerging within the Vietnamese equity market: the VN-Index continues to hold at elevated levels, but this masks deteriorating breadth underneath. Market gains are being driven almost exclusively by a narrow group of large-cap stocks — primarily banking names and Vingroup — while the majority of listed equities remain flat or in correction. This classic "green index, red market" (xanh vỏ, đỏ lòng) dynamic is a key risk signal for international fund managers. Average daily liquidity in 2026 has hovered around VND 26,000 billion per session, materially lower than the active periods of prior years. Foreign investors continue to be net sellers, adding further pressure. Kafi Securities' Director of Analysis, Luong Duy Phuoc, cautions that the VN-Index level alone is not a reliable proxy for market health; true market strength requires broad-based profit generation across the majority of stocks. For equity-exposed funds, this concentration risk warrants close monitoring. A genuine recovery would require expanding breadth, a pickup in liquidity, and a reversal in foreign net selling — none of which are currently present.

---

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of June 27 — Survey Across MB, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, HDBank, Sacombank and Others
medium.summary: A survey of online deposit rates as of June 27 shows ACB leading the market at 7.3% per annum for the 12-month tenor, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% p.a. A cluster of banks — including MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, and VIB — are offering 7.0% p.a. for 12-month deposits, while the state-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) continue to maintain stable, lower rate schedules. The persistence of relatively elevated deposit rates at private banks (7.0–7.3% range) suggests ongoing competition for retail funding, which could place upward pressure on lending rates and squeeze net interest margins if sustained. For bond market participants, elevated deposit rates at private banks serve as a competing benchmark and may dampen demand for government bonds at the shorter end of the curve if deposit yields remain attractive on a risk-adjusted basis.

medium.title: Next Week: One Bank to Lock in Dividend Rights at Nearly 30%
medium.summary: KienlongBank (KLB) has announced July 3, 2026 as the record date for shareholders to receive a stock dividend at a rate of 29.5% — one of the highest dividend ratios in the banking sector this year. The bank plans to issue over 170 million new shares, increasing its charter capital from VND 5,822 billion to over VND 7,537 billion, with prior SBV approval already secured. While this is primarily a corporate action rather than a systemic event, the capital raise is notable for banking sector watchers as it reflects continued SBV encouragement of bank recapitalization to support credit expansion targets. Equity investors in Vietnamese bank stocks should note the ex-dividend date and potential share price adjustment for KLB.

medium.title: Contradictory Phenomenon Unfolding in the Stock Market — What Do Experts Say?
medium.summary:
The VN-Index is being propped up by a narrow group of large-cap stocks — predominantly banking shares and Vingroup — while the broader market remains weak, creating a "green on the surface, red beneath" dynamic. Average daily liquidity in 2026 has held around VND 26 trillion per session, materially below levels seen during the 2021–2022 bull market, signaling cautious money flows. Foreign investors continue to be **net sellers**, adding to the lack of broad market momentum. Kafi Securities' Head of Analysis, Luong Duy Phuoc, cautions that index levels alone do not reflect true market health, and that three specific catalysts would be needed to break the current stalemate. **Relevance:** Persistent foreign net selling is a key indicator of capital outflow pressure, which has direct implications for VND demand and the balance of payments. Fund managers should monitor whether the VN-Index's index-level resilience masks deteriorating breadth that could precede a sharper correction.

---

medium.title: Vietnam's Shrimp Exports Near $2 Billion: U.S. and China Competing for Supply, Vietnam Holds World-Leading Processing Technology
medium.summary: Vietnam's shrimp exports reached $1.9 billion in the first five months of 2026, up 12% year-on-year, according to VASEP (Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers). China and Hong Kong emerged as the dominant growth driver, with exports to that market surging 46% YoY to over $711 million — nearly 38% of total shrimp export value — supported by strong demand for frozen shrimp and lobster products. Meanwhile, exports to the United States declined, falling to $228 million over the same period, continuing to represent a headwind for the sector. From an FX and macro perspective, this robust export performance is a modest positive for USD inflow generation and Vietnam's current account position. Sustained export momentum in seafood, combined with other commodity categories, supports the trade surplus narrative that helps underpin VND stability. Fund managers should monitor whether U.S. tariff risks or demand softness could weigh on the U.S. channel in H2 2026, which could partially offset China-driven gains.

medium.title: Vietnam Receives Very Positive News from China and the U.S. — Rattan and Bamboo Exports Sustain Growth Momentum
medium.summary: Vietnam's rattan and bamboo export sector generated nearly $400 million in the first five months of 2026, up 8.6% year-on-year, with China posting particularly strong growth of over 53% compared to the same period in 2025. The United States remains the largest single market, accounting for over $190 million — nearly half of total sector exports — representing 10.7% YoY growth. Monthly exports in May 2026 were approximately $80.9 million. While this is a niche export category, the broad-based demand across both China and the U.S. markets contributes incrementally to Vietnam's overall trade surplus and USD inflow dynamics. For FX-focused investors, continued diversification of Vietnam's export base across multiple major economies provides a degree of resilience to bilateral trade shocks and supports the current account, which remains a key pillar of VND stability in the medium term.

medium.title: MBS Research: Historical Data Shows World Cup Season Is Not a Golden Period for Vietnamese Equities
medium.summary: In its latest market report, MB Securities (MBS) notes that the VN-Index has recovered toward the 1,900-point level, but the headline index masks significant underlying weakness — for every stock advancing, five are declining, creating a divergence between index performance and actual portfolio returns. Market liquidity has fallen into depressed territory, though MBS highlights that this deterioration is occurring without negative spillover from global equity markets and that net foreign selling pressure has meaningfully eased. MBS characterizes the current environment as one of excessive investor caution and "indifference" toward a series of pivotal macro policy shifts, arguing that these structural measures — including infrastructure project acceleration and removal of economic bottlenecks — will not deliver immediate results but will compound over time into tangible GDP growth. The easing of foreign net selling is a marginally positive signal for international fund managers monitoring capital flow dynamics, as sustained foreign outflows have been a persistent headwind for the VN-Index and for VND stability. Watch for whether liquidity recovers as the World Cup period concludes and whether foreign flows turn neutral-to-positive.

medium.title: Gold Price Plunge Alarms Investors — Fund Managers Reveal What the Market Is Overlooking
medium.summary: Global gold prices have fallen below $4,500/oz and are testing long-term support at the 200-day moving average. The near-term selling pressure is attributed to rising inflation expectations, which are increasing the probability that major central banks — including the Fed — could raise interest rates later in the year. Higher-for-longer rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets such as gold, driving capital rotation into yield-bearing instruments. However, Tom Winmill of the Midas Discovery Fund cautions against over-indexing on short-term corrections, arguing that structural fundamentals supporting gold remain intact, particularly given ongoing central bank accumulation dynamics globally. For VND and Vietnamese bond market watchers, this is contextually relevant: if the Fed pivots toward rate hikes rather than cuts, USD strength would intensify, placing renewed upward pressure on USD/VND and potentially forcing the SBV into further FX intervention or reserve drawdowns. This also reduces the case for near-term SBV rate cuts.

medium.title: New Personal Income Tax on Gold Bar Trading Effective July 1, 2026
medium.summary:
Starting July 1, 2026, Vietnam's Personal Income Tax Law 2025 (Law No. 109/2025/QH15), passed by the National Assembly in December 2025, takes effect. A key new provision classifies income from the transfer/sale of gold bars (vàng miếng) as taxable income. The government retains authority to set the taxable threshold value, applicable dates, and tax rate adjustments in line with its gold market management roadmap. For non-resident individuals, the tax base is calculated on the transfer price of gold.

**Relevance for traders:** Vietnam's gold market is closely linked to VND dynamics and SBV intervention. By introducing personal income tax on gold bar transactions, the government aims to formalize and cool speculative activity in the physical gold market — a persistent source of VND pressure when domestic gold premiums spike and attract capital away from financial assets. This regulatory tightening could reduce arbitrage demand for USD to fund gold purchases, marginally supportive of VND stability. Watch for the government's implementing decree to clarify tax thresholds and rates, which will determine actual market impact.

medium.title: Top 15 Largest Companies in Southeast Asia: Vingroup and Vinhomes Make the List, Surpassing Names from Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia
medium.summary: According to CompaniesMarketCap data, Vingroup has risen to 4th place among Southeast Asia's largest companies by market capitalization at approximately USD 65 billion (~VND 1.7 quadrillion), while its subsidiary Vinhomes also entered the top 15 at USD 25 billion. This places Vingroup ahead of regional blue chips including Singtel, Sea Limited, and UOB. Singapore's DBS Group leads the regional ranking at USD 144 billion. The milestone reflects the growing maturity and scale of Vietnam's equity market and the rising weight of Vietnamese private conglomerates in regional capital market benchmarks — a factor that increasingly influences foreign portfolio flows into the VN-Index.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of 28 June: Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank...
medium.summary:
A survey of online deposit rate schedules across 34 Vietnamese banks as of 28 June shows the overall rate environment remains largely stable with limited movement. The majority of banks are posting 12-month deposit rates in the 6.8–6.9% per annum range, with only six institutions offering 7% or above for the 12-month tenor. ACB leads the market at 7.3% p.a. for 12 months, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% p.a., while MBV, PGBank, VCBNeo, and VIB all offer 7.0% p.a. The concentration of higher rates among smaller and mid-tier banks suggests the big four state banks (Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) continue to hold rates lower, reflecting their stronger liquidity positions. For VND and bond market participants, the sticky deposit rate floor around 6.8–7.3% provides a key benchmark for pricing government bond yields at the short-to-medium end of the curve; any broadening of the 7%+ cohort would signal tightening liquidity conditions worth monitoring.

---

medium.title: Silver Plunges Nearly 10% in One Week: Fed Becomes the Biggest Headwind for Precious Metals
medium.summary: Silver prices collapsed sharply over the past week, with domestic Vietnamese silver (Phú Quý) ending the week at approximately VND 59.87M/kg (buy) and VND 61.71M/kg (sell), down ~8.7% week-on-week. Internationally, spot silver closed at USD 59.19/oz (-8.77%), while COMEX September futures lost over 10% and Shanghai exchange silver dropped nearly 14% in a single week. The primary driver cited is a significant hawkish repricing of Fed expectations following hotter-than-expected US PCE inflation data — now at its highest level in over three years — alongside an upward GDP revision for Q1. **Relevance to VND traders:** A more hawkish Fed narrative reinforces USD strength broadly, which historically adds depreciation pressure on the VND. This development, combined with elevated US inflation prints, may delay any Fed easing cycle and keep USD/VND elevated. Fund managers should monitor upcoming SBV intervention signals and whether the central bank will be compelled to defend the VND more actively if USD strength persists into Q3 2026.
